Ban on employer use of automated decision systems.
Various mental health and insurance matters.
Civil liability for child sexual abuse material.

reading.body:
Indiana's tracked bills include a ban on employer use of automated decision systems and a pair of near identical bills on digital sexual image abuse, alongside a civil liability bill for child sexual abuse material, but most of the remaining bills, health claims payment, property tax, education matters, and foreign adversary registration, do not concern AI directly.

The employer automated decision systems ban stands out as Indiana's clearest AI specific labor policy, addressing algorithmic management in hiring or workplace decisions as a distinct legal category from the digital image abuse and child protection bills filed the same week in January 2026.

Two bills, HB1182 and HB1183, share the identical title "Digital sexual image abuse," a duplication pattern that in other states' bill lists reflects companion or competing versions of similar legislation introduced separately, though this record does not clarify their relationship.

The data does not indicate which of these 13 bills passed, failed, or remain pending, nor does it include bill text beyond title and number, so Indiana's actual enacted AI and digital abuse framework is not established by this record.
